newsitem.title: USA: ADM in $30 million settlement of securities suit.
newsitem.headline: ADM in $30 million settlement of securities suit.

text.p: Archer Daniels Midland Co. agreed to pay $30 million to settle a shareholders' class-action lawsuit related to its involvement in an alleged price-fixing scheme, a lawyer for the shareholders said Friday.
Although it agreed to settle the suit, ADM did not admit guilt in the matter, said Lester Levy, the shareholders' lead counsel.
In a statement released from its headquarters in Decatur, Ill., ADM acknowledged that it reached the settlement.
The lawsuit alleged that as a result of the alleged price-fixing scheme, ADM's revenues were inflated and as a result, shareholders had paid inflated prices for the stock.
The price-fixing allegations evolved from a Justice Department investigation into sales of a feed additive called lysine, as well as citric acid and high-fructose corn syrup, a sweetener.
ADM acknowledged on Thursday that the corporation and two of its top executives might be indicted as a result of the investigation.

ADM also said it agreed to settle for $35 million a separate class-action antitrust lawsuit filed against it in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California. The suit involved the sale of citric acid.
